title: Global aspects of the Cauchy problem in general relativity

verification.evidence: Springer abstract: 'It is shown that, given any set of initial data for Einstein's equations which satisfy the constraint conditions, there exists a development of that data which is maximal in the sense that it is an extension of every other development. These maximal developments form a well-defined class of solutions of Einstein's equations. Any solution of Einstein's equations which has a Cauchy surface may be embedded in exactly one such maximal development.'

notes: Foundation for the MGHD object used throughout the ledger (D-007/D-008).

title: Naked singularities in the Einstein-Euler system

verification.evidence: Springer abstract: 'In 1990, based on numerical and formal asymptotic analysis, Ori and Piran predicted the existence of selfsimilar spacetimes, called relativistic Larson-Penston solutions, that can be suitably flattened to obtain examples of spacetimes that dynamically form naked singularities from smooth initial data, and solve the radially symmetric Einstein-Euler system. ... We provide a rigorous mathematical proof. ... we reformulate the problem in double-null gauge to flatten the selfsimilar profile and thus obtain an asymptotically flat spacetime with an isolated naked singularity.'

notes: Matter model: Einstein-Euler (perfect fluid), radially symmetric, asymptotically flat. Rigorous counterpart of the dust/fluid naked-singularity family.

title: A robust proof of the instability of naked singularities of a scalar field in spherical symmetry

verification.evidence: Springer abstract: 'Published in 1999, Christodoulou proved that the naked singularities of a self-gravitating scalar field are not stable in spherical symmetry and therefore the cosmic censorship conjecture is true in this context. The original proof is by contradiction and sharp estimates are obtained strictly depending on spherical symmetry. In this paper, appropriate a priori estimates for the solution are obtained. These estimates are more relaxed but sufficient for giving another robust argument in proving the instability, in particular not by contradiction.'

notes: Confirms and stabilizes T-101's scope (instability in spherical symmetry, cosmic censorship 'true in this context'). arXiv ID 1710.02922 verified by the lead on 2026-09-12; the abstract does not itself use the term 'bounded variation' (that wording comes from review C2 and is not adopted as verified).

title: Instability of spherical naked singularities of a scalar field under gravitational perturbations

verification.evidence: Lehigh University abstract: 'In this paper, we initiate the study of the instability of naked singularities beyond spherical symmetry. ... It is shown that, arbitrarily fixing the initial scalar field, the set of the initial conformal metrics on the outgoing null cone such that the maximal future development does not have any sequences of closed trapped surfaces approaching the singularity, is of first category in the whole space in which the shear tensors are continuous. ... the set of the initial conformal metrics such that the maximal future development has at least one closed trapped surface before C_epsilon, contains an open and dense subset of the whole space. ... we may say that the spherical naked singularities of a self-gravitating scalar field are not stable under gravitational perturbations.'

notes: Key non-symmetric perturbation result; genericity here is 'first category' for the exceptional (no-trapped-surface) set and 'open and dense' for the censoring set - a third genericity vocabulary in the ledger.

title: A construction of approximately self-similar naked singularities for the spherically symmetric Einstein-scalar field system

verification.evidence: Springer abstract: 'In this work, we identify stable perturbations of k-self-similar naked singularities, in the full parameter range k^2 in (0,1/3). As a consequence, we provide a dynamical construction of naked singularity interior and exterior regions outside of exact self-similarity ... This data is required to satisfy conditions consistent with the absence of a blue-shift instability and is therefore non-generic. The argument combines a backwards stability argument in the interior region with a global existence problem in the exterior region, adapting techniques developed by Rodnianski and Shlapentokh-Rothman ... to the spherically symmetric setting.'

notes: Explicitly non-generic (fine-tuned/vanishing-to-high-order) perturbations. Another data point for D-006.
